rows.evidence: Q1: Introduction and Methodology sections <U+2013> the brief reports an ADB pilot demonstration activity in the Lower Bari Doab Canal (756,000 ha) that processed Landsat/Sentinel imagery with SEBAL for 2017<U+2013>2018 to compute 15 irrigation performance indicators per distributary and rotation cycle; Main Findings and Table 2 report its own Gini coefficients of delivered water and division-level water deficit results.
rows.notes: The study diagnoses inequity rather than demonstrating that remote sensing improves it. Its own results are: Gini coefficients showing canal delivery was more equitable in Kharif than Rabi (Main Findings); division-level differences in canal supply, consumptive use and crop water deficit (Table 2); and the design of a prototype DSS that reallocates canal water among divisions and distributaries. No change in equity resulting from use of the remote sensing information is measured <U+2013> the DSS is only proposed, the PID 'has decided to continue developing the prototype', and the conclusion speaks of 'scope to improve'. The claimed effect (improving equity) is therefore only a downstream possibility of what the study shows (measuring inequity and generating recommendations), so Q2 is 'no' and upstream is set. The claim's word 'essential' is also not an own finding. Note the brief itself lists limitations (no ground validation, only one year of satellite data) and the Gini/IPI results carry no dispersion measures, but these are not scored because Q2 is 'no'.

notes: The document is an 8-page ADB policy brief condensing a technical assistance study report; figures (2<U+2013>5) are referenced but their content is not reproduced in the text, and numerical results are limited to Table 2. Treated as primary because it reports the project's own satellite-derived indicator results, but the level of methodological detail is low.
